programme.title: Anton Chekhov 1890
programme.desc: Anton Chekhov, a humble Russian doctor, writes novels he sells to newspapers to feed his family. As his talent gets noticed by his peers, Chekhov even gains Tolstoy’s admiration. But when his brother dies from tuberculosis, Chekhov, remorseful, decides to flee his escalading notoriety and travels to the penal colony of the Sakhalin Island, in Siberia, to write about the depraved society the convicts live in. This journey will inspire some of his most brilliant and famous pieces.

programme.title: Discovering Film: Ed Harris

programme.title: Moulin Rouge

The Italian city of Florence, as prestigious as it may be, is in a very embarrassing situation: its immense cathedral, under construction for more than a century, still has no dome. At this time, no one has found a solution for constructing what will be the widest and highest dome ever built.

But when his brother dies from tuberculosis, Chekhov, remorseful, decides to flee his escalading notoriety and travels to the penal colony of the Sakhalin Island, in Siberia, to write about the depraved society the convicts live in. This journey will inspire some of his most brilliant and famous pieces.

The Italian city of Florence, as prestigious as it may be, is in a very embarrassing situation: its immense cathedral, under construction for more than a century, still has no dome. At this time, no one has found a solution for constructing what will be the widest and highest dome ever built.

But when his brother dies from tuberculosis, Chekhov, remorseful, decides to flee his escalading notoriety and travels to the penal colony of the Sakhalin Island, in Siberia, to write about the depraved society the convicts live in. This journey will inspire some of his most brilliant and famous pieces.

programme.title: Faking Influence
programme.desc: The Feed continues its investigation into the murky world of social media influencers. This week, journalist Calliste Weitenberg tries everything to grow her fake Instagram account - from fake tan to awkward bikini selfies. But with her follower count staying stubbornly low, she turns to dodgy websites that offer fake followers for cash. Will she get caught? Or has Calliste just bought her way into the $15 billion influencer marketing industry?

programme.title: High Society
programme.desc: 'Basuco' is now considered the cheapest drug in the world at 20 cents a hit. It's made from the residue leftover from cocaine production, mixed with brick dust, volcanic ash, sulphuric acid, kerosene and sometimes ground-up human bones. The high is all-consuming and shockingly addictive, and an epidemic of basuco dependency is tearing through poor communities all across South America.

programme.title: High Society
programme.desc: Crystal meth has never been a European problem. For years, reports of the drug ravaging communities and fuelling week-long binges almost exclusively came from North America and South-East Asia. But there are increasing signs that meth is becoming much more popular in cities from Barcelona to Berlin.

programme.title: High Society
programme.desc: All across the UK gangs are using teenagers to sell drugs in the country. Some victims as young as 12 are violently coerced into a terrifying form of modern slavery. Nequela Whittaker is a former county lines runner who sold drugs in the countryside. Now out of prison, she tells her story of meeting kids who are current or former victims, and police trying to combat it.
